scope.description: A non-exclusive directory of mathematical works and resources for translation outside maintained project lanes. Each row gives a readable work identity, language evidence, distribution class, and practical next action.
scope.coverage_rule: A row is a suggestion unless a packaged job and public readback say runnable. Unknown coverage means unknown, not absence; current maintained editions are not adoption targets unless explicitly listed.

language_priority.priority_rule: Any language is welcome. Contributors may consider communities in the UNESCO-UIS 96-language assessment set and other underserved languages; record the exact locale, script, written standard, intended learners, and existing coverage.

education_access_source.title: New UNESCO report calls for multilingual education to unlock learning and inclusion
reported_facts: 40% of people globally lack access to education in a language they speak and understand fluently.
More than a quarter-billion learners are affected.
Only 351 of roughly 7,000 spoken or signed languages are used as a medium of instruction.

uis_96_language_study.title: Benchmarking by Language Groups Framework

cited_study.title: Inadequate foundational decoding skills constrain global literacy goals for pupils in low- and middle-income countries

reported_facts: The cited study covered 96 languages using alphabetic writing systems across 48 low- and middle-income countries.
The UNESCO-UIS report describes 75% of the study assessments as conducted in a local or national language and 25% in English, French, Spanish, or Portuguese.
uis_96_language_study.label_note: Labels are preserved as printed in Table S1. They are not normalized ISO identifiers; resolve the current language name, locale, script, and written standard with the intended community before starting a translation.
uis_96_language_study.translation_use: This evidence set supplies concrete candidate language communities, not a ranking or a closed queue. Verify current educational need and work-specific coverage before choosing one.

language_priority.note: The UNESCO education-access figures and the UNESCO-UIS 96-language study are distinct evidence. The 96-language study is real, but it is a literacy-assessment set rather than a fixed UNESCO translation-priority list.

separate_archive.warning: This is a separate older-manuscript corpus. Its rows and aggregate language tags are not coverage for the open-education suggestions.
